headline: Brent -2% overnight, France held at Aa3, Brazil ETF -18%, S&P futures +0.4%, FOMC Oct 28
stance: Both weekend risks passed: France kept its rating, no Iran strike. Relief bid into FOMC Oct 28 and 3 hyperscaler prints; AI credit is the live stress.

news.head: SpaceX closed $40bn of GPU debt; record IG deal next
news.body: Musk, Sunday: SpaceX borrowed on its investment-grade rating and non-AI revenue. Debt markets 'almost entirely shut' to pure-AI borrowers, he said.

news.head: Meta -9.4% last week after its print; CDS +22bp
news.body: 5y CDS 127bp. Free cash flow was negative in the quarter despite the beat. The market priced the capex, not the earnings.

news.head: SK Hynix: ~$12bn special dividend reported
news.body: +4% Friday. Shareholder-return plan due Wednesday, on about 80% of the Kioxia stake proceeds. Reports this week, with Samsung.

news.head: Amex: EPS beat, revenue miss, 5% of staff cut
news.body: EPS $4.68 ex-gain vs $4.48; revenue $20.06bn vs $20.12bn. Full-year EPS guide raised to $18.30-18.60. -3.6% by midday Friday. Beats still sell.

implications: Oil and France both de-escalated overnight; neither is resolved. Strike risk moves to after the Nov 3 midterms; French unions have called a Nov 5 strike.
AI stress now prices in CDS, not only in equity. Capex guides Oct 28-29 decide whether the year's largest IG supply clears.

watch.head: 2y auction today; FOMC Oct 28, 2pm
watch.body: Hold 91% priced, December hike 80%. Chair Warsh presser 2:30. ECB Oct 29; BoJ Oct 30, hold at 1.25% expected with a December hint.

watch.head: Earnings: Microsoft, Alphabet Oct 28; Amazon Oct 29
watch.body: All after the close. Consensus revenue: Microsoft $90.6bn, Alphabet $128bn, Amazon $202bn. Capex guides outrank the FOMC for the AI trade.

watch.head: GDP and PCE Oct 29, 8:30
watch.body: PCE consensus: headline +0.5% m/m, core +0.3%. Q3 GDP advance the same morning. Durables and new home sales tomorrow; employment cost index Friday.

watch.head: Iran: 'decision time'; US forces at 96-hour readiness
watch.body: Trump ruled out a Sunday strike. Qatari mediators in Tehran Sunday. 28 Hormuz attacks in October, a record month; 122 ships on Iran's non-compliance list.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Brent $114.40, -2% (~3am ET), off Friday's highest close since April; WTI $100.85. Trump Sunday: 'no strike today'. Gold $4,015 (~4am ET), -4% last week, worst since June.
Moody's held France at Aa3 Friday night; a cut was the consensus. French 10y 4.94% (~6am ET), OAT-Bund 157bp from 178bp last week. Euro 1.1210 (~4am ET), little changed.
Lula re-elected Sunday, 51.8-48.2; Bolsonaro contesting. Brazil ETF -18% overnight (~10pm ET), real -10% in futures. The right-wing-win trade unwinds at today's open.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 20: WTI specs 14th percentile, new this week, with WTI itself at the 99th percentile of 3 years. Funds are not long this oil rally. Silver specs 8th, -13 points on the week.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Futures (~4:30am ET): S&P +0.4%, Nasdaq 100 +0.6%. Stoxx 600 +0.3%, DAX +0.7% (~4am ET). Kospi -0.8% to a 3-month low; Hang Seng +0.7% (~2:30am ET).
Friday: staples led the S&P lower, energy led up. Week: S&P -0.5%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Dow +0.4%. Chipmakers posted their longest run of weekly losses since November.
3 hyperscalers, ~15% of S&P weight, report Wednesday and Thursday after the close. Each moved 10% or more on at least 1 print this year.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 20, unchanged 4 to 5 weeks: Russell 2000 specs 100th percentile, Nasdaq 100 97th, VIX shorts 4th. Standing background into the hyperscaler prints, not a new development.

single_name.note: NextGen Infrastructure Income Fund: 2 insider-buy rules fired, filing dated Oct 23, new to the list today. Above its 200-day. Long setup, score 4 of 5.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Neocloud 5y CDS 1,146bp Friday, +19bp on the week; the group -2.5% in Sunday overnight trading. Single-name CDS is where AI stress trades now.
Funding is not the stress: SOFR-OIS and CP spread sit at calm levels while CDS gaps. This is a credit-selection widening, not a liquidity one.
Supply is the next test: the 2 largest IG deals of the year are reported in preparation. Spreads absorb that or they do not; capex guides Oct 28-29 set the bid.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 20: HY bond specs 13th percentile, new this week, -15 points. Dealer IG inventory 19th percentile. Thin books on both sides into record supply.
